subject: Dedicated pool sizing & vendor ETA — need synchronized fulfillment windows
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Hao Li <hao.li@orca-cloud.com>, procurement@orca-cloud.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing & vendor ETA — need synchronized fulfillment windows

Hao / procurement team —

Thanks again for sending the updated quote last week. Nimbus is requesting an anchor of 180 A100-equivalent GPUs for their Dedicated pool tied to deal D-2027-0891. Before we commit we need a clear fulfillment plan that aligns three things: OEM manufacturing ETAs, cloud partner capacity (burst/backstop) availability, and our internal staging/onboarding windows.

Key asks from Redwood side:
- Confirm OEM lead time ranges for the 180-unit tranche and for a +30% buffer (i.e., 234 units) — we need earliest/likely/latest dates and any conditional dependencies (component shortages, allocation holds).
- Confirm whether your quote assumes single-shipment vs. phased deliveries and the min tranche size.
- Provide a cloud partner backstop offer (region: us-west-2) and whether that capacity is soft-reserved or requires additional contractual commit.
- Any constraints on firmware/OS imaging or shipping to our staging hubs that might add 2–4 weeks.

We have an internal deadline to finalize commitments by EOD Aug 31 to hit the Q4 onramp. If you can send a short delivery cadence (CSV or bullet list) + updated DocuSign-ready SOW, we can review immediately. Attaching the previous quote for reference.

[Attachment: nimbus_oem_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)]

Thanks,
Diego
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Hao Li <hao.li@orca-cloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orca-cloud.com
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing & vendor ETA — need synchronized fulfillment windows

Diego —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick summary from our side after checking with manufacturing and our cloud partner ops:

OEM manufacturing ETAs (best / expected / worst):
- 180 units: 12 / 16 / 24 weeks from PO receipt.
- 234 units (+30% buffer): 14 / 20 / 28 weeks from PO.

Notes: lead times are driven primarily by GPU die allocation (third-party wafer scheduling) and a backlog on power-supply subassemblies. We can push for prioritization but it will require a short-term premium (~4% on list).

Delivery cadence options we can support:
1) Single shipment (full) — available only on the "expected" timeline and requires a fixed manufacturing window (higher risk on worst-case).
2) Phased (recommended): 60/60/60 for first three tranches over 12–16 weeks, remainder as buffer. Minimum tranche we can ship is 30 units.

Cloud partner (us-west-2) backstop:
- We have soft-reserved capacity for 75 equivalent GPUs that can be contracted for a 3-month bridge. Procurement must sign a short addendum; pricing shown in cloud_capacity_terms.xlsx.
- For larger bursts we can broker additional slots but lead time is ~2–4 weeks to confirm (depends on partner acceptance).

Imaging/shipping constraints:
- Standard firmware image is supported; custom image embedding adds 5–10 business days.
- Customs/port variability could add 7–12 days on the long tail.

I attached a proposed phased delivery schedule and the updated capacity terms. I can run this by the factory to try and shorten the worst-case window if you confirm a reserved commit on the 180 tranche.

[Attachment: cloud_capacity_terms.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)]

Best,
Hao
Supply Ops Manager — Orca Cloud

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated pool sizing & vendor ETA — need synchronized fulfillment windows

Team — forwarding Orca's note. Short summary and action items:

Summary: Orca gives us phased delivery (recommended) with 12–16 week expected lead for 180 units; worst-case 24 weeks. They can soft-reserve 75 GPUs in us-west-2 for a 3-month bridge but it requires an addendum. Manufacturing can try to compress worst-case if we take a price premium or sign earlier.

My recommended approach for the deal:
1) Contractually anchor the 180-unit tranche but split it into a 60/60/60 phased shipment (reduces single-shipment risk).
2) Sign the cloud backstop addendum for 75 GPUs to guarantee product availability during the first 12 weeks of onboarding. Cost justified as bridge to avoid missing Nimbus's Q4 go-live.
3) Negotiate OEM premium cap (max 4%) and include a firm latest delivery date with liquidated damages tied to SLA (we need Ops advise on enforceability).

Questions for Karthik / Procurement:
- Can Procurement commit to a PO with phased payment tied to receipt milestones? If yes, what's the minimum acceptance terms we can accept (net days, inspection window)?
- If we take the 3-month cloud backstop, are there budget/contract implications for the customer that should be presented now?

Attachments: Orca's terms + my suggested SOW edits (SOW draft attached).

[Attachment: sow_draft.docx (DOCX, 3 pages)]

Diego

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 10:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool sizing & vendor ETA — need synchronized fulfillment windows

Diego / Team —

Thanks for the summary — couple of procurement notes and a suggested path:

Procurement stance: we can issue a PO with phased payment tied to delivery milestones (receipt + acceptance testing). Typical terms we can accept for strategic OEMs: Net 60 with a 10-business-day inspection window and 2% holdback. We should avoid open-ended "worst-case" clauses without capped exposure.

Cloud backstop: approving a 3-month soft reservation for 75 GPUs looks reasonable from a risk perspective but we need customer approval on passing through the incremental cost; recommend we include the backstop as an optional line-item in the SOW and have Nimbus sign-off.

Commercial ask for sales: if we're committing to the PO this week, we should negotiate a staged cancellation window (e.g., ability to cancel tranche 3 without penalty up to X days prior) and reserve the right to accelerate tranche shipment if Nimbus pre-pays. That gives us flexibility without full exposure.

Next steps (recommended):
1) Diego to get Nimbus sign-off on including the cloud backstop as an optional SOW addendum.
2) I will prepare PO terms reflective of Net60 + 2% holdback and include tranche cancellation language.
3) Marissa / Vanessa — please prepare a short customer-facing note that explains bridging with the cloud backstop and the optional premium. Keep it simple: timeline impact, cost delta, and recommended acceptance.

Karthik
Director, Procurement — Redwood Inference
